Daily Devotional

December 5

15 And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust. 16 And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men. (Acts 24:15-16 KJV)

This was where Paul was defending himself in front of the Governor, and was refuting that he had committed any offence. Paul was bringing up the resurrection of the dead, as it was a item of contention among the Pharisees and the Sadducees, who were the ones persecuting him. By causing the two sects to breakup, then he hoped to get off the hook. This verse does tell us that Paul believed that all people would be resurrected - both the believers and unbelievers. Some believe that only a select few will be resurrected, but the bible teaches that all will be brought back, the First Resurrection of the just (Revelation 20:5), and then the unsaved (Revelation 20:14-15) to face the White Throne Judgment (Revelation 20:11). Those written in the book of life will be with Jesus for eternity, and the others cast into the lake of fire, which is the second death (Revelation 20:13-14). The bible teaches in many places that no one ceases to exist, but that our souls live forever, either on the new earth, or in the lake of fire. I believe I would rather live forever with Jesus than the devil, and in the New Jerusalem, rather than the lake of fire.

Note that Paul said he exercised his conscience to keep from having any offence toward God or man. You can exercise your conscience, and must do so, to keep it clear of any offences. We must continually purge our conscience to keep it from condemning us (Romans 8:1), as the devil will try to work condemnation in you all he can, as he is the master of lies and evil deeds (John 8:44). The devil’s favorite tool is to make you feel condemned and unworthy of God’s blessings. To overcome his tactics, you must put all your faith in Jesus, and when the devil tries to put condemnation on you, just agree with him that you are not worthy, but thank God for Jesus, who has given you His righteousness, and that will always shut the devil up. Just remember that the devil is a liar, and His weapon against the saints is lies and deceit. If you keep your focus on Jesus at all times the devil is powerless. The wiles of the devil consist of evil thoughts, lies, and deception, as he has no real power other than those things. Praise God for Jesus giving us power over the enemy (James 4:7).
